definition: very probable; used for predictions
example: It is highly likely that the release will slip to next week.
exampleEs: Es muy probable que el lanzamiento se retrase a la próxima semana.
cloze: It is ____ likely that the release will slip to next week.
note: Use 'highly' with likely, unlikely, recommended, effective. Not 'very very very'.

definition: worried in a serious, strong way
example: The team is deeply concerned about the security of the new API.
exampleEs: El equipo está profundamente preocupado por la seguridad de la nueva API.
cloze: The team is ____ concerned about the security of the new API.
note: Concerned about + noun, not 'concerned of'.

definition: useful to a very high degree
example: This debugging tool is extremely useful when the logs are messy.
exampleEs: Esta herramienta de depuración es extremadamente útil cuando los logs están desordenados.
cloze: This debugging tool is ____ useful when the logs are messy.
note: Replaces 'very, very, very good': one strong adverb is enough.

definition: completely tired, with no energy left
example: After the all-night deployment, I was utterly exhausted.
exampleEs: Después del despliegue de toda la noche, estaba completamente agotado.
cloze: After the all-night deployment, I was ____ exhausted.
note: Utterly goes with extreme words (exhausted, ridiculous), not with plain 'tired'.

definition: to depend on something a lot
example: Our pipeline heavily relies on a single third-party service.
exampleEs: Nuestro pipeline depende mucho de un solo servicio de terceros.
cloze: Our pipeline ____ relies on a single third-party service.
note: Always 'rely ON', never 'rely in'.

definition: very disappointed and upset
example: The founders were bitterly disappointed when the investors pulled out.
exampleEs: Los fundadores quedaron amargamente decepcionados cuando los inversionistas se retiraron.
cloze: The founders were ____ disappointed when the investors pulled out.
note: Bitterly is for negative feelings only.

definition: to recommend with a lot of conviction
example: I strongly recommend that we test this before the demo.
exampleEs: Recomiendo encarecidamente que lo probemos antes de la demo.
cloze: I ____ recommend that we test this before the demo.
note: After 'recommend that', use the base verb: 'recommend that we test'.

definition: to believe something with total certainty
example: I firmly believe that small habits beat big plans.
exampleEs: Creo firmemente que los hábitos pequeños superan a los planes grandes.
cloze: I ____ believe that small habits beat big plans.
note: Good opinion opener in meetings: 'I firmly believe that...'.

definition: easy to get in many places
example: The model is widely available through several cloud providers.
exampleEs: El modelo está ampliamente disponible en varios proveedores de nube.
cloze: The model is ____ available through several cloud providers.
note: Also 'widely believed', 'widely criticized'.

definition: different in every way
example: The two teams took entirely different approaches to the problem.
exampleEs: Los dos equipos adoptaron enfoques completamente diferentes para el problema.
cloze: The two teams took ____ different approaches to the problem.
note: Entirely is not used with gradable words like 'good' or 'big'.

definition: completely conscious of something
example: I am fully aware that the deadline is tight.
exampleEs: Soy plenamente consciente de que la fecha límite es ajustada.
cloze: I am ____ aware that the deadline is tight.
note: Aware OF something, not 'aware about'.

definition: completely easy to understand
example: Her instructions were perfectly clear, so I started right away.
exampleEs: Sus instrucciones eran perfectamente claras, así que empecé de inmediato.
cloze: Her instructions were ____ clear, so I started right away.
note: Perfectly works with clear, normal, fine, reasonable.

definition: completely necessary
example: Clear communication is absolutely essential in remote teams.
exampleEs: La comunicación clara es absolutamente esencial en los equipos remotos.
cloze: Clear communication is ____ essential in remote teams.
note: Absolutely goes with extreme adjectives; not 'absolutely good'.

definition: completely not acceptable
example: Missing the client call without notice is totally unacceptable.
exampleEs: Faltar a la llamada con el cliente sin avisar es totalmente inaceptable.
cloze: Missing the client call without notice is ____ unacceptable.
note: In speech, 'I totally agree' is very common.

definition: so slow that it is frustrating
example: The old build process was painfully slow, so we replaced it.
exampleEs: El proceso de compilación anterior era dolorosamente lento, así que lo reemplazamos.
cloze: The old build process was ____ slow, so we replaced it.
note: Painfully is used for annoying or awkward qualities.

definition: really interested, not pretending
example: I am genuinely interested in how the team handles feedback.
exampleEs: Estoy genuinamente interesado en cómo el equipo maneja la retroalimentación.
cloze: I am ____ interested in how the team handles feedback.
note: Interested IN, not 'interested on'.

definition: strongly established and hard to change
example: Their fear of failure is deeply rooted in the company culture.
exampleEs: Su miedo al fracaso está profundamente arraigado en la cultura de la empresa.
cloze: Their fear of failure is ____ rooted in the company culture.
note: Rooted IN something.

definition: very sharply conscious of something
example: I am acutely aware that the budget is limited this quarter.
exampleEs: Soy muy consciente de que el presupuesto es limitado este trimestre.
cloze: I am ____ aware that the budget is limited this quarter.
note: More formal than 'very aware'; good for meetings.

definition: to remember in clear, detailed images
example: I vividly remember my first day at a real software job.
exampleEs: Recuerdo vívidamente mi primer día en un trabajo real de software.
cloze: I ____ remember my first day at a real software job.
note: 'Remember doing' = recall the event.

definition: to go up quickly and by a large amount
example: Server costs sharply increased after the launch.
exampleEs: Los costos del servidor aumentaron bruscamente después del lanzamiento.
cloze: Server costs ____ increased after the launch.
note: Good for describing charts and trends.

definition: to get better at a regular, continuous pace
example: My listening has steadily improved since I started daily practice.
exampleEs: Mi comprensión auditiva ha mejorado de forma constante desde que empecé a practicar a diario.
cloze: My listening has ____ improved since I started daily practice.
note: Present perfect for change up to now: 'has steadily improved'.

definition: to make much smaller in a big, sudden way
example: Caching can drastically reduce the response time.
exampleEs: El caché puede reducir drásticamente el tiempo de respuesta.
cloze: Caching can ____ reduce the response time.
note: Drastically goes with change words: reduce, change, cut.

definition: very competitive and determined to win
example: The AI market is fiercely competitive right now.
exampleEs: El mercado de la IA es ferozmente competitivo en este momento.
cloze: The AI market is ____ competitive right now.
note: Fiercely goes with competitive, loyal, independent.

definition: absolutely private; not to be shared
example: The clinical data is strictly confidential and cannot leave the system.
exampleEs: Los datos clínicos son estrictamente confidenciales y no pueden salir del sistema.
cloze: The clinical data is ____ confidential and cannot leave the system.
note: Useful in pharma and compliance contexts.

definition: easy to get immediately
example: The documentation is readily available on the internal wiki.
exampleEs: La documentación está fácilmente disponible en la wiki interna.
cloze: The documentation is ____ available on the internal wiki.
note: Readily also means 'without hesitation': 'she readily agreed'.

definition: becoming more important over time
example: Data privacy is becoming increasingly important for every product.
exampleEs: La privacidad de los datos se está volviendo cada vez más importante para todo producto.
cloze: Data privacy is becoming ____ important for every product.
note: Spanish 'cada vez más' = increasingly.

definition: different by a very large amount
example: The two proposals are vastly different in cost and scope.
exampleEs: Las dos propuestas son enormemente diferentes en costo y alcance.
cloze: The two proposals are ____ different in cost and scope.
note: Use with comparatives: 'vastly better'.

definition: good for both sides
example: We want a mutually beneficial partnership with the lab.
exampleEs: Queremos una alianza mutuamente beneficiosa con el laboratorio.
cloze: We want a ____ beneficial partnership with the lab.
note: Common in business and negotiation.

definition: to watch carefully and continuously
example: We will closely monitor the error rate after the update.
exampleEs: Vamos a monitorear de cerca la tasa de errores después de la actualización.
cloze: We will ____ monitor the error rate after the update.
note: The verb is 'monitor', not 'monitorize' (false friend).

definition: to enjoy completely
example: I thoroughly enjoyed the workshop on prompt design.
exampleEs: Disfruté muchísimo el taller sobre diseño de prompts.
cloze: I ____ enjoyed the workshop on prompt design.
note: Thoroughly also means 'carefully and completely'.

definition: to say sorry in an honest way
example: I sincerely apologize for the confusion in yesterday's meeting.
exampleEs: Me disculpo sinceramente por la confusión en la reunión de ayer.
cloze: I ____ apologize for the confusion in yesterday's meeting.
note: Apologize FOR something, to someone.

definition: wrong at the most basic level
example: The experiment design was fundamentally flawed from the start.
exampleEs: El diseño del experimento estaba fundamentalmente defectuoso desde el inicio.
cloze: The experiment design was ____ flawed from the start.
note: A strong critique phrase for reviews.

definition: to think about something carefully as a real option
example: You should seriously consider asking for a clearer scope.
exampleEs: Deberías considerar seriamente pedir un alcance más claro.
cloze: You should ____ consider asking for a clearer scope.
note: Consider + -ing: 'consider asking'.

definition: to choose after thinking
example: We need to make a decision before Friday.
exampleEs: Necesitamos tomar una decisión antes del viernes.
cloze: We need to ____ a decision before Friday.
note: Spanish 'tomar' is not 'take' here: 'make a decision'.

definition: to do something that might fail
example: Startups have to take a risk to grow quickly.
exampleEs: Las startups tienen que correr un riesgo para crecer rápido.
cloze: Startups have to ____ a risk to grow quickly.
note: Also 'run the risk of' + -ing.

definition: to focus on something
example: Please pay attention to the error messages in the logs.
exampleEs: Por favor presta atención a los mensajes de error en los logs.
cloze: Please ____ attention to the error messages in the logs.
note: Pay attention TO, not 'pay attention in'.

definition: to bring up a worry so others discuss it
example: I want to raise a concern about the testing timeline.
exampleEs: Quiero plantear una preocupación sobre el calendario de pruebas.
cloze: I want to ____ a concern about the testing timeline.
note: Raise needs an object; 'rise' does not.

definition: to do research in an organized way
example: The team will carry out research on user retention next month.
exampleEs: El equipo llevará a cabo una investigación sobre la retención de usuarios el próximo mes.
cloze: The team will ____ out research on user retention next month.
note: Formal alternative to 'do research'.

definition: to organize and run a survey
example: We conducted a survey to learn what users actually want.
exampleEs: Realizamos una encuesta para saber qué quieren realmente los usuarios.
cloze: We ____ a survey to learn what users actually want.
note: Stress: con-DUCT (verb) vs CON-duct (noun).

definition: to finish something on time
example: The whole team worked hard to meet the deadline.
exampleEs: Todo el equipo trabajó duro para cumplir con la fecha límite.
cloze: The whole team worked hard to ____ the deadline.
note: 'Cumplir' = meet; not 'fulfill the deadline'.

definition: to decide after thinking or discussing
example: After two hours, the committee reached a conclusion.
exampleEs: Después de dos horas, el comité llegó a una conclusión.
cloze: After two hours, the committee ____ a conclusion.
note: 'Arrive at' also works, but not 'arrive a conclusion'.

definition: to form an opinion from evidence
example: It is too early to draw a conclusion from this data.
exampleEs: Es muy pronto para sacar una conclusión de estos datos.
cloze: It is too early to ____ a conclusion from this data.
note: Spanish 'sacar una conclusión' becomes 'draw', not 'take out'.

definition: to organize and run a meeting
example: We will hold a meeting with the clinical team on Monday.
exampleEs: Llevaremos a cabo una reunión con el equipo clínico el lunes.
cloze: We will ____ a meeting with the clinical team on Monday.
note: In casual speech, 'have a meeting' is also fine. Not 'make a meeting'.

definition: to present something to an audience
example: She will give a presentation about the new model.
exampleEs: Ella dará una presentación sobre el nuevo modelo.
cloze: She will ____ a presentation about the new model.
note: Spanish 'dar' maps well to 'give' here.

definition: to decide what you want to achieve
example: I set a goal to pass the exam in six months.
exampleEs: Me fijé la meta de aprobar el examen en seis meses.
cloze: I ____ a goal to pass the exam in six months.
note: Past of set is also set.

definition: to deal with something difficult
example: Every new developer will face a challenge like this one.
exampleEs: Todo desarrollador nuevo enfrentará un desafío como este.
cloze: Every new developer will ____ a challenge like this one.
note: Face has no preposition: 'face a challenge', not 'face with'.

definition: to succeed in dealing with a difficulty
example: They overcame many obstacles to get approval for the study.
exampleEs: Superaron muchos obstáculos para obtener la aprobación del estudio.
cloze: They ____ many obstacles to get approval for the study.
note: Past tense is irregular: overcome, overcame, overcome.

definition: to have a part or influence in something
example: Communication plays a key role in remote teams.
exampleEs: La comunicación desempeña un papel clave en los equipos remotos.
cloze: Communication ____ a key role in remote teams.
note: Also 'play an important role in' + noun.

definition: to move forward or improve
example: We are making progress on the migration.
exampleEs: Estamos avanzando en la migración.
cloze: We are ____ progress on the migration.
note: 'Progress' is uncountable: never 'a progress'.

definition: to execute a test
example: Let me run a test on the new build.
exampleEs: Déjame ejecutar una prueba en el nuevo build.
cloze: Let me ____ a test on the new build.
note: Common in tech: run a script, run a query.

definition: to slowly create trust
example: Honest updates help build trust with stakeholders.
exampleEs: Las actualizaciones honestas ayudan a generar confianza con los interesados.
cloze: Honest updates help ____ trust with stakeholders.
note: 'Stakeholders' is a common meeting word.

definition: to find a fair middle point between two things
example: It is hard to strike a balance between speed and quality.
exampleEs: Es difícil encontrar un equilibrio entre velocidad y calidad.
cloze: It is hard to ____ a balance between speed and quality.
note: Balance BETWEEN two things.

definition: to start a lively discussion
example: The announcement sparked a heated debate in the community.
exampleEs: El anuncio desató un debate acalorado en la comunidad.
cloze: The announcement ____ a heated debate in the community.
note: Great for Discord and online community topics.

definition: to help explain something
example: The report sheds light on why users leave in the first week.
exampleEs: El informe aclara por qué los usuarios se van en la primera semana.
cloze: The report ____ light on why users leave in the first week.
note: Shed is irregular: shed, shed, shed.

definition: to be a possible danger
example: Weak passwords pose a serious threat to the whole system.
exampleEs: Las contraseñas débiles representan una amenaza seria para todo el sistema.
cloze: Weak passwords ____ a serious threat to the whole system.
note: Pose a threat TO something.

definition: to say a worry out loud
example: Several engineers voiced concerns about the new schedule.
exampleEs: Varios ingenieros expresaron preocupaciones sobre el nuevo calendario.
cloze: Several engineers ____ concerns about the new schedule.
note: Voice is also a verb here, not only a noun.

definition: to deal with a problem
example: We need to address this issue before the audit.
exampleEs: Necesitamos abordar este problema antes de la auditoría.
cloze: We need to ____ this issue before the audit.
note: 'Address' means 'deal with', not 'give someone an address'.

definition: to compare good and bad points before deciding
example: Let's weigh the pros and cons before choosing a vendor.
exampleEs: Sopesemos los pros y contras antes de elegir un proveedor.
cloze: Let's ____ the pros and cons before choosing a vendor.
note: Weigh sounds like 'way'.

definition: to do what you said you would do
example: If you make a promise, you must keep it.
exampleEs: Si haces una promesa, debes cumplirla.
cloze: If you make a promise, you must ____ it.
note: The opposite is 'break a promise'.

definition: to stop doing something you usually do
example: It took me months to break the habit of checking my phone.
exampleEs: Me tomó meses romper el hábito de revisar mi teléfono.
cloze: It took me months to ____ the habit of checking my phone.
note: Habit OF + -ing.
